orders.reason: Falls on warfarin, gait change, forgetfulness
Gait disorder, falls, cognitive change, urinary urgency

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Gait and Memory Change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his daughter, who asked for the visit. Over the past few months he has started shuffling his feet, and he's fallen several times at home - no head strike he remembers, no injuries. She thinks he's more forgetful: repeating questions, lost track of a bill. He also sometimes doesn't make it to the bathroom in time, which embarrasses him. He minimizes all of it but agrees the walking is worse. No headache, no new weakness or numbness, no dysuria or fever. Hip itself painless.

Exam: Alert, conversational, a bit slow with dates. Gait: wide-based, short shuffling steps, slow to get started, turns in several steps. Strength full in all four limbs, sensation intact. No tremor. Regular rhythm, mechanical click, AS murmur unchanged. R hip ROM painless.

A/P: Several months of gait disturbance with falls, cognitive slowing and urinary urgency in a 73 y/o on warfarin.
- Head CT without contrast now - falls on anticoagulation, and to look at ventricles/structure.
- UA to exclude infection as a driver of the urgency. TSH, B12, BMP, CBC.
- Neurology referral.
- Home safety: remove loose rugs, night lights, grab bar in the bathroom; daughter will help set up. Cane at all times for now.
- Warfarin continued - benefit for the mechanical mitral valve outweighs fall risk; reviewed with both of them.
Will call with CT.

events.reason: Head CT for gait change and falls on warfarin

reports.text:
Technique: axial non-contrast images of the head.
Comparison: none.
Findings: The lateral and third ventricles are enlarged. The cortical sulci are normal in size. No intracranial hemorrhage. No extra-axial collection. No mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved; no acute infarct. Basal cisterns patent. Calvarium intact. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged ventricles with normal cortical sulci. No hemorrhage or acute intracranial abnormality.

documents.title: Head CT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt and daughter (on speaker). No bleeding on the CT. The fluid spaces in the brain (ventricles) are enlarged while the surrounding brain looks normal - together with his walking, memory and bladder symptoms this raises the question of normal pressure hydrocephalus. Neurology appointment is 5/14; I sent them the CT. If neurology wants a spinal tap we'll need to hold warfarin - will plan once they tell us.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/14/2024
Referring: primary care

73-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis and a mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, accompanied by his daughter. She describes several months of shuffling, multiple falls at home and increasing forgetfulness, with some episodes of not reaching the toilet in time.

PMH: as per referral - HTN, DM2, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, mechanical MVR, severe AS, right hip arthroplasty with revision 2023.
Meds: warfarin (held for today's procedure, enoxaparin bridge), lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, aspirin 81.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Alert, oriented to person and place, approximate on date. MMSE 24/30 (lost points on recall and orientation). Cranial nerves intact. Strength 5/5 throughout, no sensory deficit, reflexes symmetric. Gait broad-based with a 'magnetic' quality - feet seem stuck to the floor, marked difficulty initiating steps, slow multistep turns.

Imaging: head CT 04/18/2024 reviewed - enlarged ventricles with normal cortical sulci.

Procedure: High-volume lumbar puncture, L3-4, after confirming INR below threshold. Clear CSF removed without complication. Timed walk and gait observation before and 2 hours after: noticeably quicker start, longer steps, fewer steps to turn. Improvement was temporary by the end of his visit window, as expected.

Assessment: Normal pressure hydrocephalus, with a positive response to CSF removal.

Plan:
1. Neurosurgery referral to consider a ventriculoperitoneal shunt.
2. Resume anticoagulation per PCP plan tonight.
3. PT for gait and fall prevention.
4. Return after neurosurgical evaluation.

cc: PCP

OUTSIDE NEUROSURGERY - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 06/11/2024

73M referred by neurology with gait apraxia, cognitive slowing and urinary urgency; head CT with ventriculomegaly and normal sulci; clear gait improvement after a large-volume tap on 05/14. Mechanical mitral valve on warfarin; severe aortic stenosis, followed by cardiology; DM2; CKD 3.

Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: magnetic, broad-based gait; slow turns. Strength and sensation intact.

Impression: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus, tap-responsive. Good candidate for shunting.

Plan: Right ventriculoperitoneal shunt with a programmable valve, scheduled 07/23/2024. Anticoagulation to be held with bridging - PCP to coordinate (warfarin off 5 days, enoxaparin last dose 24 h before; heparin post-op once cleared). Risks including bleeding, infection, over-drainage and shunt malfunction discussed with patient and daughter; they wish to proceed. Avoid strong magnets near the valve; any MRI needs valve check afterward.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - NEUROSURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 07/23/2024  Discharge 07/25/2024

Diagnosis: Normal pressure hydrocephalus.
Procedure 07/23/2024: Right frontal ventriculoperitoneal shunt with programmable valve. Uncomplicated.

Post-op CT head: catheter tip in good position in the right lateral ventricle; no hemorrhage.

Course: Unremarkable. Up walking POD1 with PT - steps longer and steadier than pre-op. Heparin infusion started POD1 evening once cleared, warfarin restarted POD1. Incisions clean. Valve setting documented in the operative note; wallet card given.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge meds: home medications unchanged; enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h until INR >= 2.5 per PCP.
Disposition: home with daughter, outpatient PT.
Follow-up: neurosurgery 6 weeks; PCP INR within 1 week. Call for headache, vomiting, fever, wound drainage or worsening gait.

Functional: independent ADLs; daughter now helps with bills and checks the pill box weekly. Not driving long distances.

Reviewed problem list, meds (unchanged), NKDA, family/social history.

Exam: vitals as charted. Shunt incisions healed. Harsh systolic murmur RUSB, mechanical click. Lungs clear. No edema. Gait: wide-ish but much quicker to start than in April, turns in 3 steps. Feet intact.

Prevention: flu/COVID in October. Pneumococcal, Shingrix, RSV done. Eye exam - optometry visit next month. Colonoscopy normal Jan 2024.
Advance directive on file; health care proxy is his daughter.

Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, UACR, INR (A1c was done in July).
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Rectal Bleeding
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called back after INR draw this AM (INR in range). For about a month he's had spells of bright red blood with his bowel movements, lasting a day or two then stopping on their own. No pain. No black stools. No lightheadedness beyond his usual, no fainting. Bowels otherwise his usual.

On warfarin + ASA for mechanical MVR. Colonoscopy normal in January.

Plan: GI referral placed, urgent - they have 11/27. Continue warfarin and aspirin for now given the valve. Go to ED for heavy bleeding, clots, dizziness or fainting, or black stools. CBC at GI.

events.reason: Recurrent painless bright red blood per rectum

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/27/2024
Referring: primary care

HPI: 74-year-old man with a mechanical mitral valve on warfarin and aspirin and a history of colon polyps (normal surveillance colonoscopy 01/2024). Over the past month he has had recurrent painless bright red blood per rectum, each episode lasting one to two days and settling without treatment. No abdominal pain, no diarrhea, no weight loss, and his bowel pattern is no different from usual.

PMH: severe aortic stenosis, HTN, DM2, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, NPH s/p VP shunt 07/2024, chronic constipation, right hip arthroplasty.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg, aspirin 81 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg, amlodipine 5 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: no colorectal cancer; no hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

Exam: T 36.8 C, BP 128/70, P 80, RR 14. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Rectal: gross blood on the glove, no palpable mass.

Labs: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, MCV 82 fL.

Assessment: Intermittent painless hematochezia with anemia on anticoagulation. Ddx includes angioectasia, diverticular bleeding, hemorrhoidal or rectal source.

Plan: Diagnostic colonoscopy 12/10 during a quiet period; PCP to arrange warfarin bridging. If bleeding recurs actively, ED for tagged red cell scan. Continue warfarin and aspirin pending evaluation.
